question: A team keeps arguing about whether Claude's drafts of their monthly service report are good enough, and each reviewer reaches a different verdict. What would most improve how they evaluate the drafts?
options: A) Asking for two drafts each month and adopting whichever of the two the reviewers prefer once they compare them.
B) Writing down what a complete report must contain before the draft is produced, and reviewing against that list.
C) Agreeing that a draft passes when a clear majority of the reviewers involved consider it good enough to publish.
D) Appointing the most experienced reviewer to make the final call whenever the reviewers disagree about a draft.
correct_answers: B) Writing down what a complete report must contain before the draft is produced, and reviewing against that list.
explanations: Comparing two drafts identifies the better of the two, which may still fall short of what the report actually needs to contain.

Correct. Disagreement of this kind comes from reviewers applying different unstated standards. A written statement of what the report must contain turns the review into a check against something specific instead of a matter of taste.
Voting aggregates opinions formed on different criteria, so it produces a decision without producing a shared standard.
Deferring to seniority settles arguments without making the standard explicit, so the same disagreement returns every month.
